sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +12 days over 5 years while revenue compounded -4.0%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.
Current Ratio Liquidity: Current assets cover current liabilities 1.16 times. Liquidity is tight relative to short-term obligations.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 12.8 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.

Payout Ratio Sustainability: Dividends absorbed 120% of earnings against free cash flow of 184% of net profit. The payout is above what the business generates, so it depends on cash reserves or borrowing.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 6.9% with ROE of 9.0% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 128 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 4 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 28 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded 2.9% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 6 hard red flags and 2 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 43/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
